# `Q-13-14` — Invalid link-external-filter

> The `link-external-filter` option is not a regular expression
> Quarto can compile, so it is ignored.

## What this means

`link-external-filter` tells Quarto which absolute links count as
*internal* when `link-external-icon` or `link-external-newwindow`
is on. Any link whose URL matches the expression is left alone.

``` yaml
format:
  html:
    link-external-icon: true
    link-external-filter: '^https://(www\.)?quarto\.org/'
```

This warning fires when the expression does not compile. The render
still succeeds. Quarto ignores the filter and falls back to the
default, which treats links under `website.site-url` as internal.
Without a `site-url`, every absolute `http(s)` link counts as
external.

## Why this happens

- **The pattern uses JavaScript-only syntax.** Quarto 1 evaluated
  this filter as a JavaScript regular expression in the browser.
  Quarto 2 compiles it with Rust's
  [`regex`](https://docs.rs/regex/latest/regex/#syntax) syntax,
  which has no look-around (`(?=…)`, `(?!…)`, `(?<=…)`, `(?<!…)`)
  and no backreferences (`\1`).
- **A typo.** An unbalanced parenthesis or bracket, or a dangling
  `\` at the end of the pattern.

## How to fix

- Rewrite look-arounds as a plain prefix match. For example, to
  treat both `quarto.org` and `posit.co` as internal, list them
  instead of excluding everything else:

  ``` yaml
  # JavaScript-only (look-ahead): rejected
  link-external-filter: '^https://(?!example\.com)'

  # Rust regex: accepted
  link-external-filter: '^https://(quarto\.org|posit\.co)/'
  ```

- Quote the pattern in single quotes in YAML so that backslashes
  reach Quarto unchanged.
- Escaping `/` as `\/` is harmless. Quarto 1's documentation
  example, `^(?:http:|https:)\/\/www\.quarto\.org\/custom`, still
  works.
